chapman_newcastle.text: Howay, chapbooks! Verse on one side, a move on the other. Canny value.

rail_guard.text: Newcastle Central, opened by Queen Victoria in 1850. Trains for every station you have visited. Mind the gap and the gannet.
All aboard! Howay, where are we off to?

then.text: Bit of rain, pet? That's nowt. Geordies go out in T-shirts in this. Howay!
Windy down the Quayside! Hold your hat, pet, the Tyne's wanting it.
Sun's out in the Toon! Everyone's down the Quayside. Canny day, this.

ncl_geordie.text: Howay, pet! Welcome to the Toon. Geordie's not hard. 'Canny' is nice. 'Bairn' is a child. 'Hadaway' is 'oh, go on, you're having me on'.
We say 'Howay the lads'. It means 'come on, then!' Everyone says it, even to the dog.

ncl_baker.text: Greggs started right here in Newcastle, in 1939, when John Gregg started delivering eggs by bike. Now it's every high street in the land.
Howay, you'll be wanting a Greggs. The sausage roll is the national treasure, and the stottie cake is a close second. Grab a bite before you tackle the Toon.

then.text: Fog on the Tyne! There's a famous song about this. The bridges are still there, honest.
Sunshine on the Tyne. All seven bridges at once, if you squint. Lovely.

ncl_guide.text: Seven bridges, a mile, and a river. There's the Swing Bridge, the High Level Bridge, the Tyne Bridge, the Gateshead Millennium Bridge, the Redheugh, King Edward VII and the Metro one.
The Tyne Bridge has its own colony of kittiwakes, the furthest inland in the world. In the season they are on a rota.

ncl_artstudent.text: The Baltic has no permanent collection, which is the idea. It changes every few months, so you never see the same thing twice. Unless you go to the cafe.
From the top floor you can see the whole Tyne, and the Sage, and a lot of seagulls auditioning.

then.text: Rain on the Town Moor. The cows don't mind. They've got coats. I've got a brolly.
Morning! Off to check on the cows. They like their breakfast early, same as me.

ncl_freeman.text: {greeting} I'm a Freeman of the City. Which gets me grazing rights on the Town Moor, among other things. I've three cows. They think they own the place, and in a way, so do I.
The Hoppings fair comes every June, the biggest travelling fair in Europe. The cows have a front row view.

then.text: Raining, so I'm under the bridge. The acoustics are canny. The pigeons agree.
Evening tune for the Quayside. The lights on the bridges come on and the seagulls go quiet.

ncl_busker.text: {greeting} Newcastle sound? Geordie folk music. Pipes: not the Highland kind, the Northumbrian kind. Smaller, gentler, played sitting down with the bellows under the arm. Posh.
Aye, a smallpipes tune can make a grown man cry. Or a seagull. Mostly the seagull.

newcastle_night_nurse.text: Off to the RVI for the night shift, pet. Flask, sandwiches, comfy shoes. Ready.
The bridges look canny lit up at night. I always stop for a minute on the way in.
Quiet out, isn't it? Get yourself home, it's past your bedtime. Nurse's orders.

newcastle_fox_watcher.text: Shh. There's a fox crossing the Town Moor. The cows don't notice. The fox doesn't care.
Newcastle's foxes are proper Geordies. Out all night, never wear a coat.
Red torch, so they're not bothered. Look, there, by the bins. Canny little thing.
